story.title: Explosion at Bolivian Military Base Leaves Two Dead and Many Missing
story.summary: An explosion at a military barracks in Viacha, Bolivia, has resulted in at least two confirmed deaths and 14 individuals reported missing. Local authorities have indicated that the death toll may rise, and they are advising the public to avoid the area due to the risk of further explosions.

explore_lenses.label: Why are nearby residents affected too?
explore_lenses.title: The blast extended beyond the barracks
explore_lenses.summary: This was not contained within a military facility: the shock waves damaged neighboring homes and forced evacuations. The immediate public-safety significance is therefore both the casualty toll and the continuing risk to civilians living beside the base.

claims.text: Officials said the explosions affected nearby homes; the Viacha mayor reported 25 affected families.
Defense Minister Ernesto Justiniano said evacuated residents would be housed temporarily at the Army Military Music School while authorities assess structural risks to damaged buildings.
Firefighters reported a remaining heat source and advised people to keep at least 150 meters from the site because of the possibility of another explosion.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about what exploded?
explore_lenses.title: A second, larger blast is still unexplained
explore_lenses.summary: Authorities have described two detonations rather than one. They link the first provisionally to stored pyrotechnic material, but say the material and cause of the larger second explosion require technical investigation.

claims.text: Defense Minister Ernesto Justiniano said the first detonation appeared to involve black powder from stored pyrotechnic material, while the cause and material involved in the second, larger explosion remained under investigation.

Police subcommander Roger Roca said the blasts occurred in an internal area associated with training and weapons repair, but declined to identify the substance responsible before investigators report findings.
Reports place the first blast at about 2:30 p.m. on September 4, with the second occurring roughly 20 minutes later and causing the more extensive damage.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: No official technical finding had established the precise cause, whether safety protocols failed, or whether any other explosive material was involved.

explore_lenses.label: What will determine accountability and recovery?
explore_lenses.title: Search, treatment and a criminal inquiry are underway
explore_lenses.summary: The next phase combines rescue and medical care with an inquiry into possible negligence and safety failures. Early casualty figures changed substantially as authorities consolidated reports, so the final toll remains unsettled.

claims.text: The La Paz departmental prosecutor opened an investigation into suspected negligent homicide, negligent injury and other public-danger offenses, according to EFE.
President Rodrigo Paz said he ordered a thorough, technical and transparent investigation to establish the cause, check compliance with safety protocols and determine responsibility.

By late September 4, the Defense Ministry reported two confirmed deaths, seven people missing and 81 injured, including two in serious condition; earlier reports had listed 59 injured, illustrating that the figures were still being updated.

story_report.summary: Two explosions at a military barracks in Viacha, Bolivia, killed at least two people and left others unaccounted for as emergency crews warned of a possible further blast. Reports listed 14 people missing, while the Defense Ministry later reported seven missing and 81 injured, including two in serious condition, indicating that casualty figures were still being updated. The explosions also affected nearby homes, prompting evacuations and assessments of structural damage.

sections.heading: Evacuations Follow Damage to Nearby Homes
sections.body: Viacha Mayor’s Office officials said 25 families were affected by the explosions. Defense Minister Ernesto Justiniano said evacuated residents would be temporarily housed at the Army Military Music School while authorities assess the structural safety of damaged buildings. Firefighters reported a remaining heat source and advised the public to remain at least 150 meters from the barracks because another explosion remained possible.

sections.heading: Investigators Examine Cause and Responsibility
sections.body: Officials said the first detonation appeared to involve black powder from stored pyrotechnic material, while the second, larger explosion was still under investigation. Police said the blasts occurred in an internal area used for training and weapons repair, but declined to identify the substance involved before investigators issue findings. The La Paz departmental prosecutor opened an investigation into suspected negligent homicide, negligent injury and other public-danger offenses, while President Rodrigo Paz ordered a technical and transparent inquiry into the cause, safety compliance and responsibility.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not established the precise cause of the explosions, whether safety protocols failed, or whether other explosive material was involved.
The identities of the dead and the status of those reported missing had not been publicly resolved.
The total number of damaged homes and the timing of residents’ return had not been finalized.

related_stories.title: King Oyo's Body Returns to Uganda for Burial Following His Death
related_stories.summary: The body of King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, recognized as the world's youngest reigning monarch, has returned to Uganda for burial. The king passed away in the United States at the age of 34 after battling an aggressive form of cancer.

related_stories.title: Mistrial Declared in Lindsay Clancy's Murder Case After Jury Deadlock
related_stories.summary: A mistrial was declared in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial after the jury was unable to reach a unanimous decision following seven days of deliberation. The trial lasted over five weeks and included extensive testimony. Clancy's defense attorney criticized a juror for allegedly obstructing an acquittal. Patrick Clancy expressed that facing another trial would be extremely painful for the family.

related_stories.title: Rescue Efforts in Nepal Tunnel Yield Three Survivors After Floods
related_stories.summary: Rescue operations in Nepal have successfully saved three workers from a hydropower tunnel following devastating floods caused by a glacial and rock collapse on August 26. The latest rescues included a Chinese national and two others who were freed from debris after being trapped for ten days.

related_stories.title: Rescue Operations in Nepal Save Two Lives After Devastating Floods
related_stories.summary: Rescue teams in Nepal successfully pulled a Chinese man and a Nepali woman alive from debris on Saturday, 10 days after catastrophic floods struck the region. The rescues occurred in separate operations, with the man found in a hydropower tunnel and the woman rescued from her partially submerged home. Efforts continue as thousands remain missing following the disaster.
